activities.name: Chinese New Year in Chinatown
activities.note: Chinatown's street light-up and festive bazaar, with the Chingay street parade around the same time

windows.reason: the lunar new year falls between 21 January and 20 February; its first two days are public holidays

activities.name: Thaipusam procession
activities.note: devotees carry milk pots and kavadis from Sri Srinivasa Perumal Temple to Sri Thendayuthapani Temple

windows.reason: held on the full moon of the Tamil month of Thai, which falls in January or February

activities.name: Deepavali in Little India
activities.note: the festival Little India is best known for; the main day is a public holiday

windows.reason: the festival of lights falls between the second half of October and the first half of November

activities.name: Mid-Autumn Festival lanterns
activities.note: Chinatown's lanterns and celebrations are among its major annual attractions; not a public holiday

windows.reason: the 15th day of the eighth lunar month, between early September and early October

activities.name: Hungry Ghost Festival getai
activities.note: temporary song stages in residential estates, with the front row left empty for the ghosts

windows.reason: the seventh lunar month, which falls in August or September

activities.name: Singapore Grand Prix
activities.note: a Formula One night race on the Marina Bay street circuit

windows.reason: race weekend falls in late September or early October; recent editions have moved into October

activities.name: Migratory waders at Sungei Buloh
activities.note: the wetland reserve in the north-west is a stop-over on the shorebird flyway and is open all year

windows.reason: the migratory season, August to April, when waders stop over on their way south from the northern winter

activities.name: Singapore Botanic Gardens
activities.note: a UNESCO World Heritage Site open 5 a.m. to midnight every day; entry is free except for the National Orchid Garden
